claims.text: Guidance on preventing injection into documents is explicit that encoders should be applied just before rendering rather than at input time, to avoid misuse or double-encoding, and that the transformation required depends on the context the value is entering.

source.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet, OWASP Cheat Sheet Series — on encoding at output and matching the context

claims.text: The same guidance notes that where user-authored markup is intended, encoding would break the intended functionality, so sanitisation is used instead — a different operation with a different failure mode.

source.title: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet, OWASP Cheat Sheet Series — on encoding at output and matching the context

claims.text: Saltzer and Schroeder state complete mediation as: every access to every object must be checked for authority; and fail-safe defaults as: base access decisions on permission rather than exclusion.

source.title: Saltzer, J. H. and Schroeder, M. D., The Protection of Information in Computer Systems, Proceedings of the IEEE 63(9), September 1975

beats.broke: two different jobs — deciding whether a value is acceptable, and handing it safely to an interpreter — get merged into one activity called validation, and neither is then done properly
beats.fix: separate them: validate at the boundary against what you expect, and escape or parameterise at each sink for the interpreter that will read it
beats.cost: you now do both, and the second is per-destination rather than once
beats.interview: why validating input cannot be the defence against injection
